title: Substitutionary Death of Christ
definition: The substitutionary death of Christ means that Jesus died in the place of sinners, bearing what they deserved so they could receive mercy and life.
summary: Jesus died as the righteous substitute for the unrighteous.
christFocus: Christ took the place of sinners at the cross, satisfying justice and displaying love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Substitution stands at the heart of the cross. Jesus did not die merely as an example or martyr. He died for sinners, in their place.

The righteous One bore the judgment of the unrighteous so that believers could be forgiven, reconciled, and counted righteous in Him.

This doctrine magnifies both justice and love. Sin is not ignored, and sinners are not left without hope.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people carry guilt because they believe they must pay for sin themselves. Substitution matters because Christ has borne what sinners could never bear.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Trust Christ as your substitute. Stop hiding from guilt or trying to pay for sin by suffering, performance, or shame.
